corrections.why: 12.2 m is 40 feet, the height of the 1927 steel tower; the L-4 cab sat on a 50-foot pole tower in 1933, about 15.2 m

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says removed; firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the FFLA list say gone. We report both, since none gives a date or method.
Forest Lookouts lists a 75-foot pole tower at Shanghai in 1929; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts place a 75-foot pole tower at a patrol point 1/4 mile southwest. The story reports both.
firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say the 44-foot steel tower was moved from Scofield Lookout; Forest Lookouts names an Aermotor MC-40 and does not mention a move. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: The brief's L-4 design is kept. Its height of 12.2 m matches the 1927 40-foot steel tower, so the correction proposes 15.2 m for the 1933 L-4 tower; the final 1959 tower at 44 feet would be about 13.4 m if the page should describe that one instead. The annual reports for 1957-58 and 1959-60 repeat the same tower completion text, so the date is left unclear. Clearwater Timber Protective Association merged with the Potlatch association in 1966 to form Clearwater-Potlatch TPA (cptpa.com), so the record name fits the lookout's operating years. No staffing history is documented (Idaho Fire Lookouts), so staffing is left out. The site today is not described by any source read.
